transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Maya Singh (Arbor CTO); Diego Alvarez (Lead Eng); Priyanka Patel (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick hosted generation walkthrough with emphasis on streaming partials and recovery. Customer wants low-latency chat for triage workflows; concerned about PHI handling and audit logs. Redwood demo shows console, Optimize suggestions, and recommended retry strategy.

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam from Redwood inference, AE on the account. With me is Priya, she is our solutions engineer and will run the demo. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. Running a bit behind but excited.
[00:12] Diego: Yeah hi, Diego here, will be a tech side.
[00:16] Priyanka: Priyanka, product. Quick heads up, we'll be evaluating for a triage chat assistant across urgent care.
[00:22] Liam: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) quick discovery on constraints, 2) host gen streaming basics, 3) demo in the Console + Optimize suggestions, 4) retries & idempotency patterns, 5) next steps. Sound ok?
[00:34] Maya: Yep, sounds good.
[00:38] Diego: Go for it.

--- Discovery / constraints ---
[01:05] Liam: Maya, could you give a bit more color on the workload? You mentioned triage assistant — expected qps, latency targets, and data sensitivity?
[01:14] Maya: Sure. We expect maybe 30 concurrent conversations at peak, average of 0.6 requests per user per minute, but spikes up to 150 qps for short bursts. Latency target is sub-300ms for first token ideally, under 700ms for full response in typical flows. And yes — PHI will be present in some prompts. So encryption at rest and audit trails are mandatory.
[01:36] Priya: Thanks. That helps. For hosted, we can hit those latencies with appropriate model selection and low batching; we'll show tradeoffs in the demo. For PHI, Redwood offers KMS integration + SOC2 docs and private deployment options if needed.
[01:49] Diego: Quick Q: can we pin a model version and run canary? We need stable behavior across releases.
[01:55] Priya: Yes, Dedicated or Private lets you pin versions and do rollouts. Hosted also supports model pinning on a per-route basis and canary by traffic split.

--- Hosted Generation primer + streaming semantics ---
[02:20] Priya: Ok demo time. First, quick primer: hosted generation supports streaming tokens over an SSE/websocket style stream. The key things: partial responses are emitted as token slices, you can assemble them client-side, and we include a sequence index so you can detect missing chunks. For retries, important to make requests idempotent when possible — we recommend an idempotency key if you might re-POST on a network error.
[02:45] Diego: Sequence index? Is that guaranteed monotonic per request?
[02:50] Priya: Yes, within a single request stream tokens are ordered. Edge cases happen when a worker fails mid-stream and fallback kicks in; you might get partial duplication. That's why we also expose a final "done" event and token offsets. We'll show examples.

[03:22] Priya: Param walkthrough real quick: temperature controls randomness, top_p is nucleus sampling, max_tokens obviously sets response length, stop sequences can truncate. For latency you might tune max_tokens and use stream-first-token heuristics (like request an explanatory summary then a fuller response asynchronously).
[03:48] Priyanka: What's a good temp for deterministic triage?
[03:51] Priya: Typically 0.0-0.3 for deterministic; 0.7+ when you want variation. For triage I'd suggest 0.0-0.2.

--- Console demo: live request and streaming capture ---
[04:10] Priya: I'm switching to the Console. (brief pause) Ok, here is per-route dashboard. You can see token-level cost, latency percentiles, and error traces. I'll kick a live streaming request with a sample triage prompt.
[04:32] [04:33] Priya (typing): "Patient, 45, chest pain, onset 30 min, stable vitals. Provide likely triage steps." Sending...
[04:40] [04:41] Redwood stream: [partial] "Start with immediate vitals check, administer aspirin if suspected MI..."
[04:47] Diego: Nice — the partial came through fast. What about streaming when we do function calls? We might want structured outputs.
[04:55] Priya: We support structured output and function/tool calling semantics. You can ask for JSON output via a schema and the model will attempt to follow it; the stream will include JSON tokens which you can parse as they arrive. There can be tokenization quirks so we recommend validating on final event.

[05:28] Priya: Now showing Console's retry traces — you can see an example where an internal worker timed out and the request was retried to a fallback pool. The console shows the retry count, latency per attempt, and reason (e.g., 503 or internal OOM).
[05:45] Maya: How are retries counted for billing? Do we charge for all attempts?
[05:49] Liam: Good callout. For hosted usage we bill per token produced; retries that produce duplicate tokens will be billed. We include tooling in the Console to spot high retry rates and correlate with worker health. Optimize can recommend batching / different model shapes to reduce retries.

--- Retry/backoff & idempotency patterns ---
[06:20] Priya: Recommended pattern: set an idempotency key on requests where you can dedupe server-side, use exponential backoff with jitter client-side, and prefer safe retries for idempotent operations only. For streaming, since partial response may have been consumed, recommend using a resume token or re-fetch the final result with idempotency semantics rather than re-streaming blind.
[06:48] Diego: Any built-in resume token or KV caching?
[06:51] Priya: We have prefix KV caching for prompt prefixes and partial KV for prompt-engineered workflows so you can avoid recomputation. For stream resume, we currently suggest storing the last sequence index and asking the server for remainder; it's an area we keep improving.

[07:22] Priya: Also note concurrency knobs: adaptive batching can increase throughput but may add latency; Console exposes a per-route slider to tune batching windows. Optimize will run a profiling pass on sample traffic and recommend batch sizes and quantization that balance latency vs cost.

--- Security and compliance Qs ---
[07:50] Maya: On PHI: KMS for at-rest keys, transit TLS ofc, and are audit logs accessible to us?
[07:58] Liam: Yes, we integrate with customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports Redwood-managed KMS but you can opt into bring-your-own for Dedicated. Audit logs and token-level traces are available in the Console; we can set retention policies and export logs to your SIEM. We'll share the SOC2 and HIPAA readiness doc.
[08:17] Diego: If we do hosted first, can we later move to Private with minimal changes?
[08:22] Priya: We designed the API to be consistent across modes — same route configs and rollout semantics. You may need to reconfigure network peering for VPC/on-prem but code-level changes should be minimal.

--- Deep dive: example failure mode ---
[08:45] Priya: Demoing a failure: I'll simulate a worker crash mid-stream. (pause) You can see the stream emitted up to token 72, then we retried on fallback and resumed from a new worker. Client saw duplicate tokens 69-72 — not ideal. Our guidance: dedupe by token offsets, or prefer asking for final result again with idempotency key which returns a single canonical response.
[09:12] Diego: That duplication is tricky if our client displays live tokens. Any UI best practices?
[09:18] Priya: Yes — show a provisional partial stream, and on final 'done' event do a replace/merge with final canonical text. Also surface a transient "loading - verifying" state until finalization. For triage, maybe show high-confidence parts first and mark rest as provisional.

[09:45] Priya: Now walking through Optimize suggestions: given your sample traffic, we might recommend a 8-bit quantized variant for inference to cut cost by ~30% with small latency regress depending on model. Also suggest KV caching for prompt prefixes like system instructions. Batching windows of 10-30ms for low-latency routes, or increase to 40-80ms for heavy throughput.
[10:12] Maya: Can Optimize give us an expected RPS and cost estimate?
[10:16] Priya: Yes, in Console Optimize we can run a simulated profile; it will output tokens/sec, expected latency p50/p95 and estimated monthly cost for your sample workload. We'll run one as part of the pilot.

--- Questions from customer ---
[10:40] Priyanka: How do we handle hallucinations in triage? We need deterministic references and citations.
[10:45] Priya: Two levers: prompt engineering with conservative temperature and stop sequences; and post-filtering using classification/eval hooks. Also you can use reranking with an embedding-based retrieval to ground answers. We can demo retrieval-augmented generation in a follow-up.
[11:05] Diego: Is there a sandbox billing card or credits for the pilot?
[11:09] Liam: We typically provide free pilot credits plus a trial Dedicated burst for realistic benchmarking. We'll include details in the pricing email.

--- Recap and next steps ---
[11:35] Liam: Quick recap — Redwood will: 1) send security pack + SOC2/HIPAA notes, 2) SE to propose pilot plan and model/quantization suggestions, 3) run an initial Optimize profile using your sample traffic, 4) schedule kickoff next week.
[11:52] Maya: Sounds good. Diego will share traffic samples.
[11:56] Diego: I'll share anonymized logs and prompt samples today/tomorrow.
[12:01] Priyanka: We'll look at the pilot and align stakeholders.
[12:05] Liam: Great. Anything else before we wrap?
[12:08] Maya: No, that's it. Thanks all.
[12:12] Liam: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with docs and times.
